# XFree.in Full Published Tool Reference

This file documents only tools in the public published/indexable registry. Draft and planned tools are intentionally excluded.

---

### XML Sitemap Generator & Validator
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/xml-sitemap-generator
- **Category**: SEO & URL Tools
- **Description**: Generate valid Google & Bing XML sitemaps with priority, changefreq, lastmod, and automatic chunking for large link sets.
- **Processing**: Local processing: your URL list stays in your browser.
- **Explanation**: Converts lists of web URLs into schema-compliant XML sitemaps with proper XML escaping and sitemap index generation.
- **How to use**:
  1. Enter list of URLs line by line.
  2. Adjust priority and change frequency settings.
  3. Click generate and download sitemap.xml.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: What's the URL limit per sitemap file?**
    A: 50,000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed, per the sitemaps.org protocol. The tool auto-splits into multiple files and emits a sitemapindex.xml when you exceed either limit.
  - **Q: Do Google and Bing actually use <priority> and <changefreq>?**
    A: Google largely ignores both. Bing still reads changefreq as a hint. The tool sets sensible defaults but neither field affects rankings — the URLs themselves and their <lastmod> matter more.
  - **Q: Does it auto-generate lastmod dates?**
    A: Only if you paste them. Fabricating lastmod (e.g., setting every URL to today) is a known anti-pattern that trains crawlers to ignore your dates entirely. The tool leaves lastmod blank when no date is provided.

---

### Robots.txt Generator & User-Agent Rule Tester
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/robots-txt-generator
- **Category**: SEO & URL Tools
- **Description**: Create valid robots.txt directives for search engine crawlers, test path allowance rules, and specify XML sitemaps.
- **Processing**: Local processing: rule composition and URL testing happen in your browser.
- **Explanation**: Builds RFC 9309 compliant robots.txt files with Allow/Disallow rule groups, crawl-delay directives, and sitemap references.
- **How to use**:
  1. Add user-agent rules (e.g. Googlebot, Bingbot, *).
  2. Specify allowed and disallowed path rules.
  3. Test URL path against current rules to verify crawler permissions.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: Does the tool support wildcards and end-of-line anchors?**
    A: Yes. * matches any sequence of characters within a path, and $ anchors to the end of the URL. `Disallow: /*.pdf$` blocks everything ending in .pdf. Both are RFC 9309-compliant and understood by Google, Bing, and most modern crawlers.
  - **Q: How do multiple user-agent groups behave?**
    A: The most specific matching user-agent wins per bot. `User-agent: Googlebot-Image` takes precedence over `User-agent: Googlebot` for Googlebot-Image; `User-agent: Googlebot` beats `User-agent: *` for Googlebot. Rules do NOT combine across groups — the winning group applies alone.
  - **Q: Is robots.txt a security mechanism?**
    A: No. It's a request, not enforcement. Well-behaved crawlers respect it; hostile ones ignore it. Never rely on Disallow to protect sensitive URLs — use HTTP auth, IP allow-lists, or moving the content off a discoverable path. Robots.txt entries can even help attackers find your admin paths.

---

### Meta Tag & Open Graph Social Card Preview
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/meta-tag-generator
- **Category**: SEO & URL Tools
- **Description**: Generate meta title tags, meta descriptions, and Open Graph / Twitter Cards with real-time Google SERP and social card previews.
- **Processing**: Local processing: previews render entirely in your browser.
- **Explanation**: Constructs HTML meta tags for title, description, canonical URL, og:title, og:image, and twitter:card with length character count validation.
- **How to use**:
  1. Fill in page title, description, canonical URL, and OG image link.
  2. Inspect live Google search result snippet and Twitter/Facebook preview card.
  3. Copy generated HTML code snippet.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: What length limits does it warn about?**
    A: Title over 60 characters (Google truncates) and description over 160 characters (Google may rewrite). These are guidelines, not hard limits — Google renders titles pixel-based, not character-based, so a title with lots of narrow letters can fit more, and vice versa.
  - **Q: Why does Google sometimes show a different title in search results than the one I set?**
    A: Google may rewrite titles when it thinks it can better match user intent — using your H1, anchor text pointing at your page, or metadata. Keep your <title> concise, put the primary keyword first, and match on-page content — Google is more likely to keep it.
  - **Q: Does the tool validate my og:image URL?**
    A: It checks the format (must be an absolute URL) and displays a preview if the image loads in your browser. It does NOT fetch the image server-side or check dimensions — Twitter and Facebook both cache OG images aggressively, so use their debugger tools (developers.facebook.com/tools/debug, cards-dev.twitter.com) after publish.

---

### Schema Markup Generator (JSON-LD Structured Data)
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/schema-markup-generator
- **Category**: SEO & URL Tools
- **Description**: Generate valid Schema.org JSON-LD structured data for WebSite, Organization, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, Article, and Breadcrumbs.
- **Processing**: Local processing: JSON-LD is generated in your browser and never uploaded.
- **Explanation**: Generates rich snippet structured data in valid JSON-LD format with form validation and Google Rich Results compliance checks.
- **How to use**:
  1. Select Schema type (e.g. WebSite, Organization, FAQPage, Article).
  2. Fill in required metadata fields.
  3. Copy formatted JSON-LD script tag.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: Which schema types can I generate?**
    A: Organization, WebSite, WebPage, SoftwareApplication, Article, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage, HowTo, and Product. Types that require visible on-page content (FAQPage, HowTo) will fail Google's Rich Results validation if you emit the schema without matching visible content — Google explicitly checks for that.
  - **Q: Can I combine multiple schemas on one page?**
    A: Yes. Wrap them in a single script with an @graph array, and give each node a stable @id. That's more compact than multiple <script type="application/ld+json"> tags and lets you cross-reference nodes (e.g., an Article publisher pointing at your Organization @id).
  - **Q: Does valid schema guarantee rich results in Google?**
    A: No. Validation is a prerequisite, not a guarantee. Google decides per-query and per-page whether to show a rich result based on content quality, indexation status, and eligibility signals. Ship correct schema and don't over-optimize.

---

### JSON / XML Formatter, Validator & Tree Viewer
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/json-formatter
- **Category**: Developer Tools
- **Description**: Format, validate, repair, minify, and inspect JSON/XML data with interactive tree views and error location diagnostics.
- **Processing**: Local processing: your JSON payload stays in the browser and is not sent to XFree.in servers.
- **Explanation**: Parses JSON and XML payloads, identifies syntax errors with line/column markers, provides formatting, minification, and visual tree hierarchy.
- **How to use**:
  1. Paste JSON or XML payload into the input editor.
  2. Toggle between Format, Minify, and Interactive Tree modes.
  3. Review validation diagnostics or click Auto-Fix for minor syntax repairs.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: Does this validate strict JSON or JSON5?**
    A: Strict JSON per RFC 8259. Trailing commas, unquoted keys, single-quoted strings, and comments are all rejected. If your source is JSON5 or JSONC, use a JSON5-aware parser instead — this tool will flag those as errors.
  - **Q: What's the largest payload I can paste in?**
    A: The tool is tested up to about 10 MB of formatted JSON. Above that, browsers slow down noticeably and Chrome tabs can be killed by the OS for memory pressure. For anything larger, use jq on the command line.
  - **Q: Will large numeric IDs lose precision?**
    A: Yes. JSON numbers are IEEE 754 doubles, so integers larger than 2^53 (9,007,199,254,740,992) silently round. If you're inspecting 64-bit database IDs or Twitter snowflake IDs, send them as strings from your API — the tool shows them exactly as received.

---

### Regex Tester & Interactive Match Explainer
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/regex-tester
- **Category**: Developer Tools
- **Description**: Test regular expressions live with match group breakdown, string replacement previews, and flags (g, i, m).
- **Processing**: Local processing: your pattern and test string stay in your browser.
- **Explanation**: Evaluates regex patterns against sample text in real-time, showing match groups, indices, and string replacement outputs.
- **How to use**:
  1. Type regular expression pattern and flags.
  2. Enter test string into input box.
  3. View highlighted matches and captured group tables.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: Which regex flavor does this use?**
    A: JavaScript (ECMAScript) regex, since it runs in your browser. That's close to PCRE but not identical — most notably, lookbehind support and Unicode property escapes (\p{...}) require a modern browser, and JavaScript has no possessive quantifiers or atomic groups.
  - **Q: Does the pattern work the same in Python or Go?**
    A: Usually mostly, but not always. Named-group syntax differs (?P<name> in Python re, ?<name> in JavaScript/Go). Character-class shorthand behavior around Unicode varies. Test in the target runtime before shipping — don't assume portability.
  - **Q: What is catastrophic backtracking and does the tool warn me?**
    A: Nested quantifiers on ambiguous patterns — for example (a+)+ or (.*)* — can take exponential time on adversarial input. The tool aborts execution after a short timeout on your test string, but it doesn't statically detect the problem. Rewrite ambiguous patterns; don't just hope your input stays benign.

---

### Bulk URL Extractor & Sitemap Generator
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/bulk-url-extractor
- **Category**: SEO & URL Tools
- **Description**: Extract URLs from massive raw text or HTML, clean, deduplicate, filter by domain, and generate valid XML Sitemaps with Sitemap-Index splitting.
- **Processing**: Local processing: input text and extracted URLs stay in your browser.
- **Explanation**: Parses raw text, HTML, or logs to isolate HTTP/HTTPS URLs, deduplicate them, filter by domain, and export Google-compliant XML Sitemaps.
- **How to use**:
  1. Paste any raw text or HTML snippet into the input area.
  2. Select domain filter, query parameter removal, and deduplication options.
  3. View real-time extracted URL stats.
  4. Download generated XML Sitemap file.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: Which URL formats does the extractor find?**
    A: Any string starting with http:// or https://, including URLs with query strings, fragments, and ports. Protocol-relative URLs (starting with //) are optionally normalized to https://. Relative paths without a base URL aren't extracted — regex-based extraction needs a full URL.
  - **Q: Does it deduplicate and strip query parameters?**
    A: Yes to dedup (default on). Query-string stripping is optional — enable it before generating a sitemap, since tracking params (utm_source, fbclid) create URL variants Google treats as duplicates of the canonical page.
  - **Q: How large an input can it handle?**
    A: Tested to about 5 MB of pasted text on a mid-range laptop. Above that, the browser tab slows noticeably. For very large log files, split them or use a command-line tool like grep -oE.

---

### Cron Expression Generator & Human Translator
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/cron-expression-generator
- **Category**: Generators
- **Description**: Generate standard 5-part cron schedule expressions, view plain-English explanations, and calculate upcoming execution times.
- **Processing**: Local processing: cron parsing and next-run calculations happen in your browser.
- **Explanation**: Translates cron syntax into human-readable sentences and calculates exact future execution timestamps.
- **How to use**:
  1. Configure minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week options.
  2. Review generated 5-part cron expression string.
  3. Inspect upcoming execution times list.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: Which cron dialect does the tool support?**
    A: Standard 5-field Unix cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. AWS EventBridge (6-field with seconds and ? placeholder), Quartz (6-7 fields), and Kubernetes CronJob all differ — the tool won't generate valid expressions for those. Kubernetes CronJob uses 5-field Unix cron, so it's compatible.
  - **Q: How does it handle DST and time zones?**
    A: The tool computes next-run times in your browser's local time zone. If your server runs in UTC, subtract accordingly. In DST-observing zones, 2am–3am either doesn't exist (spring) or exists twice (fall) — schedule at 1am or 4am to sidestep the ambiguity, or run cron in UTC.
  - **Q: Why do day-of-month and day-of-week seem to combine oddly?**
    A: In most cron implementations (Vixie cron, Kubernetes, GNU), if BOTH day-of-month and day-of-week are set (not *), the rule is OR — not AND. `0 0 15 * 1` runs at midnight on the 15th OR any Monday, not 'midnight on the 15th if it's a Monday.' Use * for one field when you want AND-like behavior.

---

### Base64 Encoder/Decoder & JWT Token Inspector
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/base64-encoder-decoder
- **Category**: Converters & Encoders
- **Description**: Safely encode and decode Base64 strings, UTF-8 text, Base64URL parameters, and inspect OAuth JWT headers, payloads, and claims.
- **Processing**: Local processing: tokens and strings are decoded in your browser and never uploaded.
- **Explanation**: Decodes JWT headers and payload claims without transmitting tokens to external servers. Supports UTF-8 safe Base64 and Base64URL encoding/decoding.
- **How to use**:
  1. Select JWT, Base64, or URL mode.
  2. Paste token or text input.
  3. View decoded header, payload claims, and expiration date.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: Is Base64 encryption?**
    A: No. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption. A Base64 string is trivially reversible with a decoder — anyone can read what's inside. Don't use it to protect secrets, credentials, or anything you'd hesitate to publish in plaintext.
  - **Q: What's the difference between Base64 and Base64URL?**
    A: Standard Base64 uses +, /, and = padding, which are all reserved characters in URL paths and query strings. Base64URL replaces + with -, / with _, and drops the padding. Use Base64URL for anything going into a URL or a JWT — the tool converts both directions.
  - **Q: Does it verify JWT signatures?**
    A: No. Signature verification requires the signing secret (HS256) or the public key (RS256/ES256) — neither should ever be pasted into a browser tool. The decoder shows the signature bytes as unverified and clearly labels it. If you need to verify, use jwt.io locally (offline) or your language's JWT library server-side.

---

### URL Slug Generator & Campaign UTM Parameter Builder
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/url-slug-utm-builder
- **Category**: Generators
- **Description**: Clean title strings into SEO-friendly URL slugs, and build campaign URLs with UTM parameters (source, medium, campaign, term, content).
- **Processing**: Local processing: slug and URL construction happen in your browser.
- **Explanation**: Converts strings into lowercase, hyphen-separated clean URL slugs while stripping special characters. Appends validated Google Analytics UTM parameters to base URLs.
- **How to use**:
  1. Type title string to generate clean URL slug.
  2. Enter destination URL and campaign UTM details.
  3. Copy final clean tracking URL.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: How does it handle non-ASCII characters in slugs?**
    A: By default it strips non-ASCII. Enable transliteration to map accented characters to their ASCII equivalents (é → e, ñ → n, ç → c). For non-Latin scripts (中文, العربية, हिन्दी) transliteration is lossy — for those, choose a slug in the target language you own.
  - **Q: Which UTM parameters does the builder support?**
    A: The five Google Analytics standard params: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content. Non-standard params (utm_id, custom keys) can be added manually to the query string but won't show in GA4's default reports.
  - **Q: What if my destination URL already has a query string?**
    A: The builder merges. Existing keys are preserved unless a UTM param has the same name (unlikely). The output uses & separators throughout — no double ? bugs.

### JSON to CSV Converter
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/json-to-csv-converter
- **Category**: Converters & Encoders
- **Description**: Convert JSON arrays or objects into consistently quoted CSV for spreadsheets, data review, imports, and local pipeline preparation.
- **Processing**: Local processing: the core transformation runs in your browser and the submitted working input is not sent to an XFree tool-processing endpoint.
- **Explanation**: Convert JSON arrays or objects into consistently quoted CSV for spreadsheets, data review, imports, and local pipeline preparation. Paste a JSON array of objects or a single object; compatible field names produce the clearest tabular columns. The tool emits quoted CSV text with a header row derived from object keys. XFree exposes this operation as a focused browser utility rather than a remote service. The implementation reuses the same tested local engine available in XFree Agent Studio, so the standalone route and Studio workflow share one transformation contract. That reduces duplicated logic and makes failures easier to reproduce. The page is designed for developers, analysts, technical writers, and SEO practitioners who need a quick result they can inspect before moving it into another system. No account is required for the core operation, and the working input remains in browser memory during normal execution. Nested objects are serialized rather than automatically flattened, so review nested values before importing the CSV. The safest workflow is to keep the original source, run a representative sample, inspect the transformed output, and then validate it against the rules of the application that will consume it.
- **How to use**:
  1. Paste or type the source value into the input editor. Paste a JSON array of objects or a single object; compatible field names produce the clearest tabular columns.
  2. Run the local “json-to-csv” engine. Processing happens in the current browser session and does not require an XFree tool API call.
  3. The tool emits quoted CSV text with a header row derived from object keys. Compare the result with the source and pay particular attention to escaping, separators, ordering, and data types that matter to your destination.
  4. Use the copy button or Ctrl+Shift+C after reviewing the result. Keep the original input available until the transformed output has been tested in its real target environment.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: What does the JSON to CSV Converter do?**
    A: Convert JSON arrays or objects into consistently quoted CSV for spreadsheets, data review, imports, and local pipeline preparation. Paste a JSON array of objects or a single object; compatible field names produce the clearest tabular columns. The transformation is deliberately narrow: it performs the named operation and returns the result without inventing extra fields or contacting an XFree processing API. This makes the tool useful for debugging, repeatable data cleanup, documentation examples, and small production-preparation tasks where you want to inspect exactly what changed before copying the output elsewhere.
  - **Q: Does JSON to CSV Converter upload my input?**
    A: No. The core transformation for JSON to CSV Converter is mapped to the XFree Studio local engine “json-to-csv” and runs in the browser. XFree may still load normal site assets and disclosed advertising resources, but the text you submit to this tool is not sent to an XFree tool-processing endpoint. For sensitive material, still review the page privacy notice and your browser extensions before pasting secrets.
  - **Q: What input should I use with JSON to CSV Converter?**
    A: Paste a JSON array of objects or a single object; compatible field names produce the clearest tabular columns. Start with a small representative sample when you are unsure of the source format, then compare the result against the original before processing a larger block. The tool does not silently repair unrelated syntax or infer missing business rules. If the input violates the engine's documented format, it returns an error so you can correct the source instead of receiving a misleading partial conversion.

### URL Component Encoder
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/url-component-encoder
- **Category**: Converters & Encoders
- **Description**: Percent-encode text as a URL component so reserved characters can safely appear inside query values, fragments, or generated links.
- **Processing**: Local processing: the core transformation runs in your browser and the submitted working input is not sent to an XFree tool-processing endpoint.
- **Explanation**: Percent-encode text as a URL component so reserved characters can safely appear inside query values, fragments, or generated links. Paste only the component you want encoded, such as a query value, rather than a complete URL unless that is intentional. The result uses browser-standard percent encoding appropriate for a single URL component. XFree exposes this operation as a focused browser utility rather than a remote service. The implementation reuses the same tested local engine available in XFree Agent Studio, so the standalone route and Studio workflow share one transformation contract. That reduces duplicated logic and makes failures easier to reproduce. The page is designed for developers, analysts, technical writers, and SEO practitioners who need a quick result they can inspect before moving it into another system. No account is required for the core operation, and the working input remains in browser memory during normal execution. Encoding a full URL as one component also escapes separators such as colon and slash, which is usually not desired. The safest workflow is to keep the original source, run a representative sample, inspect the transformed output, and then validate it against the rules of the application that will consume it.
- **How to use**:
  1. Paste or type the source value into the input editor. Paste only the component you want encoded, such as a query value, rather than a complete URL unless that is intentional.
  2. Run the local “url-encode” engine. Processing happens in the current browser session and does not require an XFree tool API call.
  3. The result uses browser-standard percent encoding appropriate for a single URL component. Compare the result with the source and pay particular attention to escaping, separators, ordering, and data types that matter to your destination.
  4. Use the copy button or Ctrl+Shift+C after reviewing the result. Keep the original input available until the transformed output has been tested in its real target environment.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: What does the URL Component Encoder do?**
    A: Percent-encode text as a URL component so reserved characters can safely appear inside query values, fragments, or generated links. Paste only the component you want encoded, such as a query value, rather than a complete URL unless that is intentional. The transformation is deliberately narrow: it performs the named operation and returns the result without inventing extra fields or contacting an XFree processing API. This makes the tool useful for debugging, repeatable data cleanup, documentation examples, and small production-preparation tasks where you want to inspect exactly what changed before copying the output elsewhere.
  - **Q: Does URL Component Encoder upload my input?**
    A: No. The core transformation for URL Component Encoder is mapped to the XFree Studio local engine “url-encode” and runs in the browser. XFree may still load normal site assets and disclosed advertising resources, but the text you submit to this tool is not sent to an XFree tool-processing endpoint. For sensitive material, still review the page privacy notice and your browser extensions before pasting secrets.
  - **Q: What input should I use with URL Component Encoder?**
    A: Paste only the component you want encoded, such as a query value, rather than a complete URL unless that is intentional. Start with a small representative sample when you are unsure of the source format, then compare the result against the original before processing a larger block. The tool does not silently repair unrelated syntax or infer missing business rules. If the input violates the engine's documented format, it returns an error so you can correct the source instead of receiving a misleading partial conversion.

### URL Component Decoder
- **URL**: https://www.xfree.in/tools/url-component-decoder
- **Category**: Converters & Encoders
- **Description**: Decode percent-encoded URL component text to inspect human-readable query values, slugs, redirect parameters, and tracking data.

- **Explanation**: Decode percent-encoded URL component text to inspect human-readable query values, slugs, redirect parameters, and tracking data. Paste a percent-encoded component such as search%20term%3Dxfree with valid percent escape sequences. The result is the decoded Unicode text represented by the component. XFree exposes this operation as a focused browser utility rather than a remote service. - **Processing**: Local processing: the core transformation runs in your browser and the submitted working input is not sent to an XFree tool-processing endpoint.
- **Explanation**: Reverse whitespace-delimited word order while preserving characters inside each token for quick text transformation and test preparation. Paste words or prose separated by whitespace. The output places the final token first and joins all tokens with single spaces. XFree exposes this operation as a focused browser utility rather than a remote service. The implementation reuses the same tested local engine available in XFree Agent Studio, so the standalone route and Studio workflow share one transformation contract. That reduces duplicated logic and makes failures easier to reproduce. The page is designed for developers, analysts, technical writers, and SEO practitioners who need a quick result they can inspect before moving it into another system. No account is required for the core operation, and the working input remains in browser memory during normal execution. Original spacing, line breaks, and punctuation attachment are not preserved because the engine operates on whitespace-delimited tokens. The safest workflow is to keep the original source, run a representative sample, inspect the transformed output, and then validate it against the rules of the application that will consume it.
- **How to use**:
  1. Paste or type the source value into the input editor. Paste words or prose separated by whitespace.
  2. Run the local “reverse-words” engine. Processing happens in the current browser session and does not require an XFree tool API call.
  3. The output places the final token first and joins all tokens with single spaces. Compare the result with the source and pay particular attention to escaping, separators, ordering, and data types that matter to your destination.
  4. Use the copy button or Ctrl+Shift+C after reviewing the result. Keep the original input available until the transformed output has been tested in its real target environment.
- **Top FAQs**:
  - **Q: What does the Word Order Reverser do?**
    A: Reverse whitespace-delimited word order while preserving characters inside each token for quick text transformation and test preparation. Paste words or prose separated by whitespace. The transformation is deliberately narrow: it performs the named operation and returns the result without inventing extra fields or contacting an XFree processing API. This makes the tool useful for debugging, repeatable data cleanup, documentation examples, and small production-preparation tasks where you want to inspect exactly what changed before copying the output elsewhere.
  - **Q: Does Word Order Reverser upload my input?**
    A: No. The core transformation for Word Order Reverser is mapped to the XFree Studio local engine “reverse-words” and runs in the browser. XFree may still load normal site assets and disclosed advertising resources, but the text you submit to this tool is not sent to an XFree tool-processing endpoint. For sensitive material, still review the page privacy notice and your browser extensions before pasting secrets.
  - **Q: What input should I use with Word Order Reverser?**
    A: Paste words or prose separated by whitespace. Start with a small representative sample when you are unsure of the source format, then compare the result against the original before processing a larger block. The tool does not silently repair unrelated syntax or infer missing business rules. If the input violates the engine's documented format, it returns an error so you can correct the source instead of receiving a misleading partial conversion.

## Workflow Recipes

- [Workflow Recipes](https://www.xfree.in/recipes): Versioned, deterministic local workflows composed from allowlisted XFree engines.
- [URL Cleanup Pipeline](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/url-cleanup-pipeline): Extract HTTP(S) URLs, normalize each URL, remove duplicates, sort the list, and export a JSON array. Steps: http-url-extract → url-normalize → line-dedupe → line-sort → lines-to-json-array.
- [Log Sanitizer](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/log-sanitizer): Trim log lines, keep ERROR lines, deduplicate repeated errors, sort them, and emit structured JSON. Steps: trim-lines → filter-lines → line-dedupe → line-sort → lines-to-json-array.
- [JWT Inspection Workflow](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/jwt-inspection-workflow): Decode a JWT without verifying its signature, format the decoded JSON, and sort object keys for inspection. Steps: jwt-decode → json-format → json-sort-keys.
- [SEO URL Audit](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/seo-url-audit): Extract and normalize links, deduplicate them, then classify URLs by the origin of the first extracted URL. Steps: http-url-extract → url-normalize → line-dedupe → classify-urls-by-first-origin.
- [JSON API Cleanup](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/json-api-cleanup): Validate JSON, format it, and recursively sort object keys into a stable review-friendly representation. Steps: json-validate → json-format → json-sort-keys.
- [Text Cleanup Pipeline](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/text-cleanup-pipeline): Trim lines, remove blanks, deduplicate repeated lines, sort the result, and count words without changing final text. Steps: trim-lines → empty-line-remove → line-dedupe → line-sort → word-count.
- [CSV Preparation](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/csv-preparation): Parse CSV into structured JSON, then serialize it back into consistently quoted CSV for a deterministic cleanup pass. Steps: csv-to-json → json-to-csv.
- [Developer Clipboard Cleanup](https://www.xfree.in/recipes/developer-clipboard-cleanup): Pull URL-shaped values out of noisy terminal or CI output, deduplicate and sort them, then export JSON. Steps: http-url-extract → line-dedupe → line-sort → lines-to-json-array.
